figures.finding: Anguilla has no performer's licence: a child (under fourteen) is under the general rule, never employed under twelve, and from twelve not before school closes, not before 6 a.m. or after 8 p.m., and not more than two hours on a school day or a Sunday; only unpaid performing in an entertainment whose proceeds go to a charitable or educational purpose is freed from the time and hours limits. The rule is about employment of any kind, so it reaches a young writer or director employed as much as a performer; the Labour Commissioner enforces it.

from12.notBefore: close of school hours on school days

value.charityException: unpaid, proceeds to charitable/educational purpose: exempt from time and hours limits

figures.applies: Anguilla; the law as at 15 December 2000 in the 2022 Revision; no regulations under s. 2(2) were found in the Revision index read.

sources.said: (a) so long as he is under the age of 12 years, but such child may be employed by his parents or guardian in domestic work at home or in light agricultural or horticultural work on the land or garden of the parent or guardian; (b) before the close of school hours on any day on which he is required to attend school; (c) before 6:00 a.m. or after 8:00 p.m. on any day; (d) for more than 2 hours on any day on which he is required to attend school; (e) for more than 2 hours on any Sunday;

(4) Nothing in paragraph (1)(c) or (d), or in any regulations made under this section, shall prevent a child from taking part without fee or reward in an entertainment the net proceeds of which are devoted to any charitable or educational purpose or to any purpose other than the private profit of the promoters. … “child” means a person who in the opinion of the court before whom he is brought is under the age of 14 years;

figures.finding: Full age is eighteen, and the Act reads 'infant' and 'minor' in every law and instrument that way; what makes a minor's contract for creative work binding (a court's approval or otherwise) and any set-aside of earnings weren't found in the Revision's laws read.

sources.said: (1) As from the commencement date, a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of 18 years instead of on attaining the age of 21 years, … (2) Subsection (1) applies for the purposes of any rule of law and, in the absence of a definition or of any indication of a contrary intention, for the construction of the expressions “full age”, “infant”, “infancy”, “minor” and “minority”
